Subject: MAP kickoff — cost/run-rate assumptions for pilot

Hi Avery / Naomi,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough yesterday. We're preparing the internal MAP and procurement packet and need a compact cost sanity check to take to finance next week. High level asks:

- Can you confirm the tokens-per-interaction assumptions you expect for our pilot (prompt vs completion split)?
- What cache-hit %, batching approach and model variant do you recommend for a low-latency clinical assistant?
- Rough tokens/$ sensitivity (optimistic / base / conservative) we should budget for first 90 days at ~200k calls/day.

Attached is our draft MAP (MAP_v1.xlsx) with the proposed milestones and a placeholder traffic profile. If you can provide a short table we can paste into the exec deck that would be ideal.

We'd also like to carve out a 2-week sim window prior to signing to validate assumptions — is that supported?

Best,
Samar Iqbal

Whitecliff Health

Thanks Samar — this is straightforward to get you. Quick summary below (will attach a concise PDF for the deck):

Assumptions (pilot baseline — "base"):
- Traffic: 200k calls/day, average request size 750 prompt tokens, expected completion 220 tokens (we used your MAP example prompts).
- Model: opt-6B-quant (production variant with cost-friendly kernels) — falls back to opt-2.7B for low-priority background jobs.
- Batching: adaptive micro-batches (target latency 95th < 300ms) with dynamic batch cap ~8 tokens per request under steady traffic, burst cap for throughput windows.
- KV-prefix cache: warm-cache hit expected ~38% during steady-state pilot. Prefetch + sticky routing used for short sessions.

Tokens/$ sensitivity (tokens per USD):
- Optimistic: 22k tokens/$ (aggressive quant + prefetch hit 55%)
- Base: 14k tokens/$ (current suggested config above)
- Conservative: 9k tokens/$ (lower cache, higher completion sizes)

Next steps we propose:
1) We produce a one-page token-econ-summary.pdf for your deck (attaching).
2) Rishi will scope a 10–14 day sim (traffic replay) using your sample traffic to validate the cache/batch assumptions and surface any token inflation points.
3) Align canary window in MAP: recommend night/weekend window for first 48h canary, then 7-day broaden.

If this looks ok I'll update your MAP spreadsheet with the numbers. Any specific SLA or cost thresholds finance needs?

— Avery

Avery — this is perfect, thanks. Two quick clarifying points before you run the sim: 

1) Caching: what do you assume for session-length distribution? Our users typically have 3–6 interaction sessions with increasing prompt context. Will that materially reduce cache hit rates?
2) Batching: are micro-batches applied per-tenant or across a pooled queue? We need to understand how latency SLAs for clinicians map to batching caps.

I've attached a short traffic sample (traffic-sample.csv) with anonymized conversation lengths — should help Rishi scope the replay. We can also carve out a small dataset with real prompts if needed under an NDA.

Samar

Thanks for the sample, Samar. Quick answers and a short ops plan below.

On Wed, 15 Sep 2026 at 10:03, Avery Johnson <avery@redwood.com> wrote:
> Assumptions (pilot baseline — "base"):
> - Traffic: 200k calls/day, average request size 750 prompt tokens, expected completion 220 tokens...

Responses:
- Session distribution: your sample shows median session length 4 interactions, tail to ~12. That pattern reduces effective cache-hit by ~6–10 percentage points vs single-turn traffic — in our sim we modeled conservative 32% warm-hit for base.
- Batching: we run adaptive batching across a tenant-pooled queue by default. Latency-sensitive routes can be pinned to a strict per-tenant flow with micro-batch cap 2–3 to keep p95 lower; cost will be ~12–18% higher for pinned lanes depending on burst characteristics.

Ops plan for validation (timeline):
- Day 0–2: ingest traffic-sample.csv, map prompts -> token distribution, identify inflation hotspots.
- Day 3–9: replay sim with three configs (optimistic / base / conservative) capturing tokens-per-minute, cache-hit, and p95 latencies.
- Day 10–14: deliver readout + tuned MAP values and a recommended canary window.

Preliminary numbers (quick sim-run estimates):
- Base config expected tokens/day: 200k * (750+220) = ~194M tokens/day -> at 14k tokens/$ ~= $13.9k/day (~$417k/month).
- Optimistic (22k tokens/$) -> ~$26.8k/month savings vs base.
- If you pin clinician-facing route (pin cap 3), expect ~15% uplift in cost on those calls; if 30% of calls are pinned, net uplift ~4.5% across total.

I'll get the sim scheduled and share a small readout deck for the MAP. Any hard budget cap finance wants to hold us to for the pilot? If we need to hit a specific monthly $ target we can iterate configs (prefetch aggressiveness, quant variant, or routing to smaller model on low-confidence completions).

— Rishi Malhotra
Principal Performance Engineer
Redwood Inference
